shared_meaning: an injury appearing as a dark mark on the skin caused by ruptured blood vessels beneath the surface
distinction_note: Bruise is standard colloquial usage; contusion is standard medical and clinical terminology.

shared_meaning: an individual or party that acquires goods or services in exchange for payment
distinction_note: Buyer is plain everyday English; purchaser is used in legal, real estate, and formal procurement contexts.

shared_meaning: the physical structure or location where a person establishes regular living quarters
distinction_note: Home carries personal, emotional connotations; residence is neutral, administrative, and legal.

shared_meaning: a four-wheeled passenger vehicle powered by an internal engine or motor
distinction_note: Car is standard conversational English; automobile is formal, technical, or regulatory vocabulary.

shared_meaning: a person who exercises managerial oversight and direct authority over workers
distinction_note: Boss is informal and conversational; supervisor is professional and organizational.

shared_meaning: a direct descendant of a biological parent
distinction_note: Child is used in everyday human contexts; offspring is used in biological, demographic, and legal contexts.

shared_meaning: a coming together of multiple people in one physical venue for a collective purpose
distinction_note: Gathering is neutral and informal; assembly denotes a formal, civic, or institutional body.

shared_meaning: a business arrangement or mutual exchange agreed upon by two or more parties
distinction_note: Deal is common conversational English; transaction is formal commercial, banking, and legal vocabulary.

shared_meaning: verbal communication or exchange of thoughts between people
distinction_note: Talk is casual everyday language; discourse is an academic and formal term.

shared_meaning: a person who has committed a crime or violated a legal statute
distinction_note: Crook is informal and colloquial; offender is standard legal, penal, and criminological terminology.

shared_meaning: an instrument or handheld object utilized to carry out a particular manual task
distinction_note: Tool is standard daily vocabulary; implement is formal, technical, and literary.

shared_meaning: a designated plot of land set aside for the burial of dead bodies
distinction_note: Graveyard is traditional and informal; cemetery is municipal, official, and professional.

shared_meaning: a liquid prepared and consumed for human hydration or refreshment
distinction_note: Drink is common conversational speech; beverage is commercial, regulatory, and culinary terminology.

shared_meaning: a person who aids or supports someone else in performing tasks or duties
distinction_note: Helper is simple everyday language; assistant is standard professional and corporate title vocabulary.

shared_meaning: items made of fabric worn to cover or protect the human body
distinction_note: Clothing is everyday vocabulary; apparel is formal, commercial, and retail industry terminology.

shared_meaning: a sensation of spinning, unsteadiness, and loss of balance
distinction_note: Dizziness is the common lay description; vertigo is the specific clinical and medical diagnosis.

shared_meaning: an authoritative principle or instruction designed to guide and govern conduct
distinction_note: Rule is a general, everyday term; regulation is formal legal, bureaucratic, and governmental language.

shared_meaning: the point in time or event marking the beginning of an undertaking or process
distinction_note: Start is plain everyday English; commencement is formal, official, and ceremonial.

shared_meaning: an itemized commercial statement of charges indicating money owed for goods or services
distinction_note: Bill is everyday consumer language; invoice is standard accounting and business-to-business terminology.

shared_meaning: financial compensation received in return for work performed or services rendered
distinction_note: Pay is common conversational language; remuneration is formal legal, financial, and human-resources vocabulary.
